items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Then I found out this guy sitting up front with the glasses was the manager. Al Colley Sully, you know.

ctx.x: someone else, Otto Hardwick. So one word led to another and so he was playing New England and he was coming back to New York. So we talked from day to day. So I decided that, well, I'd just finish this little trip, then I'd be back home, you know. Then I discovered he was going to play the Paramount (Laughs) Theater for six weeks. / So one day we were up in Hartford. There was a theater all the bands used to play on Sunday. I think it was the Star Theater, the Star Theater. All the bands, you know, they'd have a…

had any money since you've been here?" I said no. And all the fellows looked at me, you know, wondering how am I getting along. They didn't know that I'd sent home to my wife for some money in the meantime. So when I sent it -- when I sent home for the money, Johnny Hodges knew I'd -- you know, because I think he knew I'd gone to Western Union or something. So Johnny called me aside.
